Why do you question me? Ask those who heard me what I said to them. They know what I said.”
When he said this, one of the officers standing there slapped Jesus and said, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”
Jesus said to him, “If I said something wrong, testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you strike me?”
Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was standing there, warming himself. They said to him, “Are you also one of his disciples?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Did I not see you with him there in the garden?”
Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.

They brought Jesus from Caiaphas’s residence to the governor’s palace. It was early morning. They themselves did not enter the palace, so that they would not become defiled but could eat the Passover meal.
Pilate went outside to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
They answered him, “If this man were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you.”
Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your laws.” The Jews said to him, “We are not permitted to put anyone to death.”
This was to fulfill the words Jesus had spoken, indicating what kind of death he would die.
Pilate went back into the palace, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered, “Do you say this on your own, or did others tell you about me?”
Pilate answered, “Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would fight to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

Pilate said to him, “Then, if that is so, are you a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. But I was born for this very purpose and came into the world for this very purpose: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”
Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, “I find no grounds for a charge against him.”
“But you have a custom that I release someone to you at Passover. Do you therefore want me to release the King of the Jews to you?”
They all shouted, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now that Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate took Jesus and flogged him.
The soldiers made a crown of thorns, placed it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
And they came to him and said, “Hail, King of the Jews!” And they slapped him.
Pilate went outside again and said to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you so that you may know that I find no fault in him.”
Jesus came outside wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, and he said to them, “Here is the man before you.”
When the chief priests and the attendants saw him, they raised a shout and said, “Crucify him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no fault in him.”
The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to our law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God.”
When Pilate heard these words, he became even more afraid.
He went back into the palace again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said to him, “Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and authority to release you?”
Jesus answered, “You would have no authority at all over me unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore, the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”
From then on, Pilate sought to release him, but the Jews shouted, saying, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who calls himself a king opposes Caesar.”
When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat on the judgment seat at the place called the Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
It was the Friday of Passover, and it was about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Here is your king before you.”
But they shouted, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified.
They took him and led him away. Carrying the cross himself, he went out to the place called the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
There they crucified him, and two others with him, one on either side, with Jesus in the middle.
Pilate also wrote a notice and placed it on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, KING OF THE JEWS.
Many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. It was written in Hebrew, Dalmatian, and Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘King of the Jews,’ but rather, ‘He said, I am King of the Jews.’”
Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

When the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four parts, one part for each soldier. They also took his tunic, which was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.

They said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it to see whose it will be.” This was to fulfill the scripture that says, “They divided my clothes among themselves, and cast lots for my tunic.” These were the things the soldiers did.
Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” From that time on, the disciple took her into his own home.
After this, Jesus, knowing that everything was now accomplished, said, “I am thirsty,” so that the scripture would be fulfilled.
A vessel full of vinegar stood there. They filled a sponge with vinegar mixed with gall, wrapped it around a stalk of hyssop, and brought it to his mouth.
When Jesus had received the vinegar mixed with gall, he said, “Everything is accomplished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

Since it was Friday, the Jews asked Pilate to have their legs broken and their bodies taken away, so that the bodies would not remain on the crosses until the Sabbath, for that Sabbath was a great day.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man, and likewise those of the other who had been crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
The one who saw this has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks the truth, so that you too may believe.
This happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled: “Not a bone of his shall be broken.”
And again another scripture says, “They will look at the one whom they pierced.”

After this, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus in secret because of his fear of the Jews, asked Pilate for permission to take away the body of Jesus. Pilate gave permission, and they came and took it away.
Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Jesus at night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
They took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, as was the Jewish custom for burial.
There was a garden in the place where he was crucified, and in that garden was a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid.
They laid Jesus there because it was the Jews’ Friday and the tomb was nearby.
On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb early, at dawn, and sees that the stone has been removed from the entrance of the tomb.
Then she runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and says to them, “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.”
Peter and the other disciple went out and made their way to the tomb.
Both were running together, but the other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
Bending down, he sees the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go inside.
Simon Peter, who was following him, also arrived and entered the tomb, and he sees the linen cloths lying there,
and the cloth that had been on his head was not lying with the other linen cloths, but was folded separately to one side.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also entered. He saw and believed,
for they did not yet understand the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
The disciples went back to one another.
But Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping. While she was weeping, she bent down to look into the tomb
and sees two angels in white sitting where Jesus’ body had lain, one at the head and one at the feet.
They say to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She says to them, “Because they have taken my Lord out of this tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him.”
After saying this, she turned around and sees Jesus standing there, but she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus says to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?” Thinking that he was the gardener, she says to him, “Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, so that I may take him away.”
Jesus says to her, “Mary.” She turned and says to him in Hebrew, “Rabboni,” which means “Teacher.”
Jesus says to her, “Do not come near me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.’”
Mary Magdalene comes and tells the disciples that she has seen the Lord and that he said these things to her.

It was evening on the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples had gathered because of their fear of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
After saying this, he showed them his hands and his side, and the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
He says to them again, “Peace be with you. As my Father sent me, so I send you.”
After saying this, he breathed on them and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive anyone’s sins, they will be forgiven them; if you retain anyone’s sins, they will be retained.”
But Thomas, one of the Twelve, called the Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord.” But he says to them, “Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, put my finger where the nails were, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.”
Eight days later, his disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Jesus comes, although the doors were shut, and stood among them and says, “Peace be with you.”
Then he said to Thomas, “Bring your fingers and put them here, and look at my hands. Bring your hand and thrust it into my side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.”
Thomas answered and said to him, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and will believe.”
Jesus also performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples that are not written in this book.
But these things were written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that you may believe and receive eternal life in his name.
After this, Jesus again revealed himself to his disciples on the shore of the Sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself in this way:
Simon Peter, Thomas who was called the Twin, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We will come with you too.” They went and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
When morning came, Jesus was standing on the shore of the sea, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them, “Children, do you have anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.”
He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it, and they could not pull it in because of the great number of fish.
The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his garment around himself, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
The other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net with the fish, for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits.
When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire with a fish on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
Simon Peter went aboard and pulled the net ashore, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. Although there were so many, the net did not tear.
Jesus said to them, “Come and eat.” None of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” because they knew that it was the Lord.
Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
This was the third time Jesus appeared to the disciples after rising from the dead.
When they had eaten, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord, and you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
Again he said to him, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord, and you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my sheep.”

He said to him a third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” Peter was saddened because he had said to him a third time, “Do you love me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything, and you yourself understand everything, including that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.”

“Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you put on your own belt and went wherever you wished. But when you grow old, you will raise your hands, and others will put a belt on you and take you where you do not wish to go.”
He said this to indicate by what kind of death he would glorify God. After saying this, he said to him, “Follow me.”
Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them, the one who had also leaned against his chest and said, “Lord, who is the one who will betray you?”
When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
So this saying spread among the brothers, and they thought that this disciple would not die. But Jesus did not say to him, “He will not die,” but, “If I want him to remain until I come.”
This is the disciple who testifies about these things and who wrote these very things, and we know that his testimony is true.
But there are also many other things that Jesus did. If they were written down one by one, I think that even the world itself would not be large enough to hold the books that would be written.
